A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Population Transformer work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original PopT decoding experiments, efficiency and generalization studies, ablations, and analyses of learned brain representations.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical experiments and reports additional electrode-selection controls, ablations and quantitative interpretability comparisons.

M1.justification: V3 removes Gaussian coordinate fuzzing from the default model and replaces corrupted channels with activity from a randomly selected channel/time, rather than the same channel at another time. Table 8 explicitly tests the former choices as variants. Connectivity probing also changes from zero-filling a channel to omitting it. The transformer architecture and two-objective framework remain.

E1.justification: Both use the same ten-subject movie-viewing iEEG recordings, TUEG/TUAB, four auditory-linguistic tasks and pathological-versus-normal EEG classification. The new dataset citation and correction from 'seizure detection' to 'abnormal EEG detection' do not establish new coverage. Added analyses vary electrode selection or model configuration within this coverage.

E2.justification: The main decoding comparator sets remain unchanged. V3 adds best-single-channel BrainBERT to the held-out-subject comparison in Figure 6, BIOT to the resource comparisons in Tables 4–5, and fraction of significant electrodes as a functional-map comparator in Figure 12.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the reported pretraining learning rate from 1e-4 to 5e-4 and split from 98/1/1% to 89/1/10%, and revises downstream batch sizes, learning rates and schedules. Figure 7 replaces subject-count scaling on one held-out subject with data-fraction scaling evaluated across test subjects. Functional maps change from Destrieux to DKT regions. These are reported protocol changes; Figure 5 still conflicts with Appendix A over the fine-tuning batch size.

E4.justification: V3 adds random-electrode controls, TOTEM held-out-subject analysis, coordinate-fuzzing and channel-replacement ablations, and quantitative functional-map/connectivity validation. It replaces subject-count scaling with data-fraction scaling. The combined discriminative-plus-reconstruction ablation and frozen-model component ablations are removed; frozen ensemble scaling is retained as Figure 17.

E5.justification: V3 newly reports Wilcoxon rank-sum testing in Tables 1–2 and Dunnett's testing in Table 3, with significance markers and a 0.05 threshold. It also reports five fine-tuning runs for attention maps and their standard deviation in Figure 12. Cross-subject standard errors and five EEG seeds were already reported in v2; their changed numerical values do not establish increased replication.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces BrainBERT-PopT ROC-AUCs of 0.69/0.84/0.86/0.89 with 0.74/0.87/0.90/0.93. Table 2 changes TS2Vec-PopT EEG ROC-AUC from 0.8907 to 0.8883, alongside other revised scores. These accompany changed methods/settings and are not controlled same-setting gains. New results include functional-map correlation r=0.4 and connectivity correlations of 0.42–0.66, plus additional robustness and ablation results.

T1.justification: The new Algorithm 1 defines connectivity influence through absolute prediction differences, whereas v2 describes increased channel-wise loss; v3's prose still refers to loss changes. Appendix A also adds explicit loss and label formulas, with apparent BCE sign/complement errors and a '<500 ms' label condition conflicting with Section 3's '=500 ms'. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The same four contributions remain: generic pretrained channel aggregation, improved downstream decoding including held-out subjects, interpretation of learned weights, and a released usable model. The revised abstract retains the existing claims of efficient, competitive decoding across modalities and temporal encoders rather than introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: The scaling discussion now notes a plateau and suggests benefits from more diverse data, replacing the earlier explanation involving adaptation from one pretraining subject. The random-electrode analysis introduces a qualification about electrode-specific sentence-onset decodability. Appendix B narrows the parameter-efficiency comparison to 'some' end-to-end approaches after including BIOT.

D1.justification: V3 adds tensor-shape explanations, a numerical temporal criterion, connectivity pseudocode and a pointer to non-BrainBERT configuration files. It revises documented hyperparameters and recording-duration/channel-count metadata, and adds BIOT resource information. Much of the architecture, hardware, training-budget and code-access documentation already existed; the repeated repository link does not establish new availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds Bommasani et al., Brain Treebank and different anatomical-atlas references, while removing several earlier references including Parvizi and Kastner, Alexander et al. and Destrieux et al. The introduction adds an argument about downsampling in end-to-end models. The central positioning around modular aggregation of pretrained temporal embeddings remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is reframed around temporal-embedding aggregation, method explanations are expanded, and the TUAB task terminology is corrected. Temporal-encoder descriptions are grouped in the setup, and appendix headings and organization are revised. The main section sequence, contribution list and much of the explanatory narrative remain.

P2.justification: V3 replaces held-out-subject and scaling bar charts with point plots, redraws brain maps and connectivity displays, and adds robustness/comparison plots, a connectivity schematic, electrode-level matrices and new tables. Retained frozen scaling is relocated and reformatted, while the frozen-ablation table disappears. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Random-electrode controls, explicit significance testing and quantitative checks of both interpretability analyses strengthen evidence that was less directly validated in v2 (Figure 12 and Table 7). The gain is limited by removal of frozen-component and mixed-reconstruction ablations and by new documentation inconsistencies, including malformed BCE expressions and conflicting batch sizes in Appendix A and Figure 5. Higher decoding scores under revised settings are not, by themselves, evidence of better paper quality.
